newsitem.title: DENMARK: East Asiatic share up 10 pct on ship deal.
newsitem.headline: East Asiatic share up 10 pct on ship deal.

text.p: Danish trading group East Asiatic Company (EAC) shares climbed 10 percent on Wednesday on news of a divestment deal with Norwegian shipping group Tschudi & Eitzen Holding A/S.
The share traded up 13 crowns at 137 crowns at 1245 gmt.

Earlier the company announced that it had signed a declaration of intent with the Norwegian shipping group to initially take over three EAC Handymax dry cargo tankers, the bulk of its shipping activities, along with EAC's Ship Management Services.
It said that talks were planned later for Tschudi & Eitzen to take over the operation of EAC tanker vessel activities.
It declined to give any sum for the shipping divestment deal with Tschudi & Eitzen.

In a statement EAC said that the divesting of its shipping operations was part of a longterm strategy to concentrate on the group's three core areas of activity - EAC Graphics, EAC Consumer Products and EAC Food South America.
